brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.evidence: 3 full cells in a straight row (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full) with drained bins bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain etc.; long low footprint suits a windowsill; check_build clear, look shows plants visible
fill_and_plant put soil in all three bins and planted prop:1 basil-young, prop:2 mint-young, prop:3 parsley-young; look sees all three; check_build ok with no prop warnings
No tool controls sunlight; user places the low 3-cell row on a sunny sill. Drained bins suit herbs but sun itself is placement by user.

finish.summary: 3-cell straight planter with drained bins, soil, and basil, mint and parsley growing. Place on a sunny sill.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Sunny sill, three herbs — building your windowsill planter.
